paragraphs: يبدأ التقييم بالاستماع إلى قصة الشكوى: متى بدأ الألم، وما الذي يزيده أو يخففه، وهل صاحبه تورّم أو طقطقة أو شعور بعدم الثبات.

faqs.question: كيف يمكنني حجز موعد؟
faqs.answer: يمكنك الحجز عبر الاتصال الهاتفي أو من خلال واتساب، وسيتم تأكيد الموعد المناسب لك مع توضيح أي تعليمات قبل الزيارة.

faqs.question: ماذا أُحضر معي في الزيارة الأولى؟
faqs.answer: يُفضّل إحضار أي أشعة أو تحاليل سابقة، وقائمة بالأدوية التي تتناولها، وأي تقارير طبية متعلقة بالشكوى الحالية.

faqs.question: كم تستغرق الاستشارة؟
faqs.answer: تختلف مدة الاستشارة حسب طبيعة الحالة، والهدف دائمًا أن تحصل على وقت كافٍ لشرح شكواك وفهم خطة العلاج.

faqs.question: هل أحتاج إلى أشعة قبل الزيارة؟
faqs.answer: ليس بالضرورة؛ يحدد الطبيب بعد الفحص السريري ما إذا كانت هناك حاجة لأشعة أو فحوصات إضافية.

faqs.question: كيف تتم المتابعة بعد بدء العلاج؟
faqs.answer: يتم تحديد مواعيد المتابعة وفق خطة العلاج، مع تقييم التقدم وتعديل الخطة عند الحاجة.

faqs.question: هل يمكنني التواصل عبر واتساب؟
faqs.answer: نعم، يمكنك إرسال استفسارك أو طلب الحجز عبر واتساب، وسيتم الرد عليك في أقرب وقت ممكن.

faqs.question: هل يمكنني تغيير موعدي أو إلغاؤه؟
faqs.answer: نعم، يُرجى إبلاغنا مسبقًا عبر الهاتف أو واتساب حتى نتمكن من إعادة جدولة الموعد في وقت يناسبك.

faqs.question: هل سأحتاج إلى علاج طبيعي؟
faqs.answer: يحدد الطبيب الحاجة إلى العلاج الطبيعي بحسب الحالة، وغالبًا يكون جزءًا مهمًا من خطة التعافي بعد الإصابات وفي حالات آلام الظهر والمفاصل.

faqs.question: هل أتوقف عن الرياضة إذا شعرت بألم؟
faqs.answer: يُنصح بتخفيف النشاط المسبب للألم وعدم الاستمرار فيه، وطلب التقييم إذا استمر الألم أو صاحبه تورّم أو شعور بعدم ثبات المفصل.

faqs.question: هل يمكن متابعة حالتي دون زيارة العيادة؟
faqs.answer: يمكنك الاستفسار عبر واتساب، ويحدد الطبيب ما إذا كانت حالتك تسمح بالمتابعة عن بُعد أم تحتاج إلى زيارة حضورية وفحص سريري.

articles.excerpt: دليل مبسّط لفهم خشونة الركبة: كيف تبدأ، وما العلامات المبكرة التي لا يجب تجاهلها، وما الذي يمكنك فعله يوميًا لتخفيف الألم والحفاظ على الحركة.

body.text: خشونة الركبة من أكثر مشكلات المفاصل شيوعًا، خاصة بعد سن الأربعين. تحدث عندما يتآكل الغضروف الذي يغطي أطراف العظام داخل المفصل تدريجيًا، فيفقد المفصل جزءًا من نعومته وقدرته على امتصاص الصدمات.
كيف تبدأ خشونة الركبة؟
تتطور الخشونة ببطء على مدار سنوات. في البداية قد لا يلاحظ المريض سوى ألم خفيف بعد المجهود أو صعود السلم، ثم تظهر أعراض أوضح مع تقدم الحالة.

body.text: لا تتوقف عن الحركة تمامًا بسبب الألم؛ فقلة الحركة تُضعف العضلات وتزيد التيبّس. اختر نشاطًا مناسبًا وابدأ تدريجيًا.
متى تزور الطبيب؟

يُنصح بالتقييم إذا استمر الألم أكثر من بضعة أسابيع، أو صاحبه تورّم متكرر، أو أثّر على نومك أو قدرتك على المشي. يساعد الفحص السريري والأشعة على تحديد درجة الخشونة ووضع خطة علاج مناسبة قد تشمل التمارين العلاجية والأدوية، إلى جانب خيارات أخرى في الحالات المتقدمة.

articles.title: آلام أسفل الظهر: الأسباب الشائعة ومتى تقلق
articles.excerpt: معظم حالات آلام أسفل الظهر بسيطة وتتحسن خلال أسابيع، لكن هناك علامات تستدعي التقييم الطبي. تعرّف على الأسباب الشائعة وخطوات التعامل الصحيح.

body.text: يعاني أغلب الناس من ألم أسفل الظهر في مرحلة ما من حياتهم. والخبر الجيد أن معظم الحالات ترتبط بإجهاد العضلات أو الأربطة، وتتحسن تدريجيًا مع الحركة المناسبة والعناية البسيطة.
أسباب شائعة

items: شد عضلي بعد حمل شيء ثقيل أو حركة مفاجئة
الجلوس لفترات طويلة بوضعية غير صحيحة
ضعف عضلات البطن والظهر
الانزلاق الغضروفي
التغيرات المرتبطة بالعمر في الفقرات والغضاريف

body.text: ماذا تفعل في الأيام الأولى؟

items: تجنّب الراحة التامة في السرير؛ فالحركة الخفيفة تساعد على التعافي أسرع
استخدم الكمادات الدافئة لتخفيف تقلص العضلات
عدّل الأنشطة المؤلمة مؤقتًا بدلًا من إيقاف نشاطك كله
استشر الطبيب قبل تناول أي مسكنات، خاصة إذا كانت لديك أمراض مزمنة

body.title: علامات تستدعي التقييم العاجل
body.text: توجّه إلى الطبيب فورًا إذا صاحب ألم الظهر ضعف متزايد في الساقين، أو تنميل في منطقة الحوض، أو صعوبة في التحكم في البول أو البراز، أو حرارة غير مفسَّرة، أو إذا بدأ الألم بعد سقوط أو حادث.
الوقاية خير من العلاج
تساعد تمارين تقوية عضلات الجذع، والحفاظ على وزن صحي، وأخذ فترات قصيرة للحركة أثناء العمل المكتبي، ورفع الأشياء بثني الركبتين بدلًا من انحناء الظهر، على تقليل فرص تكرار الألم.
متى تحتاج إلى زيارة طبيب العظام؟
إذا استمر الألم أكثر من أربعة إلى ستة أسابيع رغم العناية المنزلية، أو كان يمتد إلى الساق، أو يتكرر بشكل يؤثر على عملك وحياتك اليومية، فالتقييم الطبي يساعد على معرفة السبب ووضع خطة علاج مناسبة.

image.alt: أخصائي يفحص أسفل ظهر مريض مستلقٍ

articles.title: الإسعافات الأولية للإصابات الرياضية: ماذا تفعل في الدقائق الأولى؟
articles.excerpt: الدقائق الأولى بعد الإصابة الرياضية تصنع فرقًا في التعافي. خطوات عملية للتعامل مع الالتواءات والكدمات، ومتى يجب التوقف وطلب التقييم.

body.text: تحدث الإصابات الرياضية في أي مستوى من ممارسة الرياضة، من المباريات الودية إلى المنافسات. والتعامل الصحيح في الدقائق الأولى يقلل التورم والألم ويساعد على تعافٍ أفضل.
أوقف النشاط فورًا
الاستمرار في اللعب بعد الإصابة قد يحوّل إصابة بسيطة إلى إصابة أشد. إذا شعرت بألم مفاجئ أو سمعت صوت فرقعة أو فقدت الثقة في ثبات المفصل، فتوقف واطلب التقييم.
خطوات الإسعاف الأولي للالتواءات والكدمات

items: الراحة: أوقف تحميل الوزن على الطرف المصاب
الثلج: ضع كمادة باردة ملفوفة بقطعة قماش لمدة 15 إلى 20 دقيقة، وكرر ذلك كل بضع ساعات في اليوم الأول
الضغط: استخدم رباطًا ضاغطًا بشكل معتدل دون إحكام زائد

body.text: العودة إلى الملعب
لا تعتمد على اختفاء الألم وحده علامةً للعودة. تحتاج العضلات والأربطة إلى استعادة قوتها ومرونتها وتوازنها أولًا، ويساعد برنامج التأهيل التدريجي على العودة الآمنة وتقليل احتمال تكرار الإصابة.

articles.title: هشاشة العظام: كيف تحمي عظامك في كل مرحلة عمرية؟
articles.excerpt: هشاشة العظام لا تظهر أعراضها غالبًا إلا مع أول كسر. تعرّف على عوامل الخطورة، ودور التغذية والنشاط البدني، ومتى يُنصح بقياس كثافة العظام.

body.text: تُبنى كتلة العظام خلال مرحلتي الطفولة والشباب، ثم تبدأ في التناقص تدريجيًا مع التقدم في العمر. وعندما يزداد هذا التناقص تصبح العظام أضعف وأكثر عرضة للكسر، وهي الحالة المعروفة بهشاشة العظام.
لماذا تُسمّى «المرض الصامت»؟
لأنها غالبًا لا تسبب ألمًا أو أعراضًا واضحة حتى يحدث كسر، وكثيرًا ما يكون في الرسغ أو الحوض أو فقرات الظهر، وأحيانًا بعد سقطة بسيطة.
عوامل تزيد من خطر الهشاشة

items: التقدم في العمر، خاصة لدى السيدات بعد انقطاع الطمث
التاريخ العائلي للهشاشة أو كسور الحوض
نقص الكالسيوم وفيتامين د
قلة النشاط البدني

body.title: قياس كثافة العظام
body.text: يساعد فحص كثافة العظام على اكتشاف الهشاشة مبكرًا قبل حدوث الكسور. اسأل طبيبك عن التوقيت المناسب لإجرائه بحسب عمرك وعوامل الخطورة لديك.
العلاج ممكن
إذا ثبت وجود هشاشة، فهناك خطط علاجية تجمع بين التغذية والتمارين والأدوية المناسبة بحسب تقييم الطبيب، بهدف تقليل خطر الكسور والحفاظ على جودة الحياة.

articles.title: الجلوس الصحيح أمام المكتب: دليل عملي لحماية ظهرك ورقبتك
articles.excerpt: ساعات العمل الطويلة أمام الشاشة من أهم أسباب آلام الظهر والرقبة. تعديلات بسيطة في مكان عملك وعاداتك اليومية قد تصنع فرقًا كبيرًا.

body.text: يقضي كثير منا ساعات طويلة يوميًا أمام الحاسوب أو الهاتف، ومع الوقت قد تتحول الوضعيات الخاطئة إلى ألم مزمن في الرقبة والكتفين وأسفل الظهر.
اضبط مكان عملك

items: اجعل أعلى الشاشة في مستوى العين أو أقل قليلًا، وعلى بُعد ذراع تقريبًا
اختر كرسيًا يدعم أسفل الظهر، أو ضع وسادة صغيرة خلفه
اجعل القدمين مستويتين على الأرض والركبتين بزاوية قريبة من القائمة
ضع لوحة المفاتيح والفأرة قريبتين بحيث يبقى المرفقان بجانب الجسم
إذا كنت تستخدم حاسوبًا محمولًا لفترات طويلة، فاستخدم حاملًا ولوحة مفاتيح منفصلة

body.text: قاعدة الحركة المنتظمة
أفضل وضعية هي الوضعية التالية؛ فالجسم لا يحب الثبات الطويل حتى في الوضع الصحيح. غيّر وضعيتك باستمرار، وخذ استراحة قصيرة للحركة كل 30 إلى 45 دقيقة.

body.title: انتبه للهاتف
body.text: النظر إلى الهاتف والرأس منحنٍ إلى الأمام يزيد الحمل على الرقبة. ارفع الهاتف إلى مستوى العين قدر الإمكان.
متى تستشير الطبيب؟
إذا استمر الألم رغم تعديل وضعيات العمل، أو صاحبه تنميل في الذراعين أو صداع متكرر، فالتقييم الطبي يساعد على معرفة السبب وتحديد العلاج المناسب.

image.alt: امرأة تعمل على حاسوب محمول وتجلس على كرسي مكتب مريح

articles.title: العلاج الطبيعي بعد الإصابات: لماذا لا تكفي الراحة وحدها؟
articles.excerpt: الراحة جزء من التعافي، لكنها ليست كل شيء. تعرّف على دور العلاج الطبيعي في استعادة الحركة والقوة، وكيف تستفيد من جلساتك إلى أقصى حد.

body.text: بعد الإصابة أو الكسر أو الجراحة، يظن كثيرون أن الراحة وحدها كافية للتعافي. لكن فترات السكون الطويلة قد تؤدي إلى ضعف العضلات وتيبّس المفاصل، وهنا يأتي دور العلاج الطبيعي.
ماذا يقدّم العلاج الطبيعي؟

items: استعادة مدى حركة المفصل تدريجيًا
تقوية العضلات التي ضعفت بسبب الإصابة أو قلة الحركة
تحسين التوازن والتحكم الحركي لتقليل احتمال تكرار الإصابة
تخفيف الألم بوسائل مختلفة يحددها المعالج
تعليمك تمارين منزلية تكمل الجلسات

body.text: تختلف مدة كل مرحلة بحسب نوع الإصابة وشدتها، ويحدد الطبيب والمعالج متى تكون جاهزًا للانتقال من مرحلة إلى أخرى.

body.title: التمارين المنزلية جزء أساسي
body.text: الجلسات وحدها لا تكفي؛ فالتزامك بالتمارين المنزلية بين الجلسات من أهم عوامل نجاح التأهيل.
كيف تستفيد أكثر من جلساتك؟

أخبر المعالج بأي ألم غير معتاد أثناء التمرين
لا تستعجل العودة إلى النشاط الكامل قبل الموعد المحدد
دوّن ملاحظاتك عن التحسن والصعوبات لمناقشتها في المتابعة

image.alt: أخصائي علاج طبيعي يساعد مريضًا أثناء تمرين إطالة

articles.title: متى تحتاج إلى أشعة الرنين المغناطيسي؟ دليل مبسّط للمريض
articles.excerpt: ليست كل آلام العظام والمفاصل بحاجة إلى رنين مغناطيسي. تعرّف على الفرق بين أنواع الأشعة، ومتى يطلب الطبيب الرنين، وكيف تستعد له.

body.text: مع انتشار الفحوصات الحديثة، يسأل كثير من المرضى عن أشعة الرنين المغناطيسي منذ الزيارة الأولى. لكن الفحص الأنسب يعتمد على الشكوى ونتيجة الفحص السريري، وليس كل ألم يحتاج إلى رنين.
الفرق بين أنواع التصوير

items: الأشعة العادية (السينية): الأنسب لتقييم العظام والكسور وخشونة المفاصل
الموجات الصوتية: مفيدة لتقييم بعض الأوتار والأنسجة القريبة من سطح الجلد
الرنين المغناطيسي: يوضح الأنسجة الرخوة بدقة، مثل الغضاريف والأربطة والأقراص بين الفقرات والأعصاب
الأشعة المقطعية: تعطي تفاصيل دقيقة للعظام في حالات معينة

body.text: متى يطلب الطبيب الرنين؟

items: الاشتباه في إصابة الأربطة أو الغضاريف داخل المفصل
ألم في الظهر أو الرقبة مصحوب بعلامات عصبية كالتنميل أو الضعف
عدم التحسن رغم العلاج لفترة مناسبة
الحاجة إلى تخطيط دقيق قبل إجراء علاجي

body.text: كيف تستعد لفحص الرنين؟

items: أخبر الطبيب إذا كان لديك منظم لضربات القلب أو أي أجهزة أو شظايا معدنية في الجسم
انزع المجوهرات والساعات والأغراض المعدنية قبل الفحص

body.title: النتيجة تُقرأ مع الفحص السريري
body.text: قد تظهر في الرنين تغيرات طبيعية مرتبطة بالعمر لا تسبب ألمًا، لذلك تُفسَّر النتائج دائمًا في ضوء الأعراض والفحص السريري، وليس بمعزل عنهما.
إذا كانت لديك أشعة سابقة، فأحضرها معك في الزيارة؛ فقد تغني عن تكرار الفحص أو تساعد على مقارنة التغيرات.

services.title: Knee and Joint Pain Treatment
services.description: Assessing the causes of knee and joint pain and building a treatment plan that suits the condition and your lifestyle.

details.lead: Knee pain is one of the most common orthopedic complaints, and it has many possible causes — from overuse and injury to joint wear and tendon inflammation. The first step is always to pinpoint the cause before choosing a treatment.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The assessment starts with your story: when the pain began, what makes it better or worse, and whether it comes with swelling, clicking or a sense of instability.
After the clinical examination, plain X-rays or an MRI may be requested when needed, and a treatment plan is then shaped around the nature of your condition and your daily activity.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Knee pain that lasts more than two weeks or keeps returning with movement
Swelling or warmth around the joint
Difficulty climbing stairs or getting up from a chair
A feeling that the knee gives way or locks as you move
Pain after a sudden injury or twist

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: Activity changes and a therapeutic exercise program to strengthen the muscles around the joint
Medication to ease pain and inflammation, as assessed by the doctor
Physiotherapy and rehabilitation sessions
Joint injections in selected cases
Discussing surgical options when conservative care isn't enough or the injury calls for it

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: Recovery time depends on the cause and the treatment chosen. Many overuse problems improve within weeks with consistent exercise, while injuries and surgical procedures need a longer rehabilitation program.
items: Follow-up visits to review progress and adjust the plan
A gradual return to activity and sport
Advice on keeping a healthy weight and protecting the joint

image.alt: A specialist examining the knee of a patient lying on an examination couch

services.title: Back and Neck Pain
services.description: Examining problems of the spine, back and neck, and telling their causes apart to choose the most suitable treatment.

details.lead: Back and neck pain can come from muscle strain or poor posture, and is sometimes linked to problems with the discs or vertebrae. Telling these causes apart is the key to the right treatment.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The assessment checks spinal movement, muscle strength, sensation and reflexes to find out whether the pain is muscular or related to pressure on a nerve.
Most back pain improves with conservative treatment; advanced imaging is reserved for signs that call for it.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Back or neck pain lasting more than a few weeks
Pain that spreads into the arm or leg
Numbness or weakness in the arms or legs
Pain that wakes you at night or gets worse at night
Pain after a fall or injury

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: Therapeutic exercises to strengthen the back and core and improve flexibility
Correcting sitting and working postures
Medication to relieve pain and muscle spasm
Physiotherapy sessions
Discussing surgery for nerve compression that doesn't respond to treatment

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: Many patients improve gradually over a few weeks when they follow their treatment plan, and keeping up the exercises helps reduce the chance of the pain coming back.
items: Regular follow-up of pain and movement
A home exercise program
Advice on a healthy work setup

image.alt: A spine model showing the lumbar vertebrae and discs

services.title: Sports Injuries
services.description: Caring for sports injuries from diagnosis through a gradual, safe return to activity.

details.lead: Sports injuries include sprains, muscle and ligament tears and cartilage injuries. Handling them correctly from the start supports a safe return to activity.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The assessment focuses on how the injury happened, how stable the joint is and how strong the muscles are, with suitable imaging when needed to identify the type and grade of injury.
The plan is built around your sporting goal: getting back to play safely while reducing the risk of re-injury.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Sudden pain during training or a match
Rapid swelling or bruising after the injury
Difficulty putting weight on the injured limb
A feeling that the joint is unstable or slipping
Pain that keeps returning when you go back to training

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: First aid and relative rest in the early phase
Temporary support with a brace when needed
A gradual rehabilitation program to restore strength and flexibility
Balance and movement-control exercises
Discussing surgery for certain ligament or cartilage injuries

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: The return to sport is divided into clear stages, and you only move on to the next stage once specific strength and movement targets are met.
items: Functional tests before returning to competition
Injury-prevention warm-up and strengthening exercises
Follow-up to adjust training loads

image.alt: An athlete wearing a knee brace next to a basketball

services.title: Fracture Diagnosis and Treatment
services.description: Managing fractures and bone injuries, and following each stage of healing step by step.

details.lead: Fractures vary in type, location and severity. Treatment depends on how stable the fracture is and on the patient's age and general health, with the aim of healing the bone in the right position and restoring function.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Fracture care begins with an examination that checks the circulation and nerves around the injury, followed by X-rays to identify the type of fracture and how far the bone has shifted.
Some fractures only need a cast, while others need to be realigned and fixed surgically, as assessed by the doctor.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Severe pain after a fall or accident
An obvious deformity or rapid swelling of the limb
Difficulty moving the limb or putting weight on it
Persistent pain in a bone after repetitive strain (stress fractures)

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: Immobilizing the fracture with a cast or brace
Realigning the fracture (reduction) when needed
Surgical fixation for unstable fractures
Pain relief and follow-up X-rays to monitor healing

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: Bones usually take several weeks to heal, depending on the type and location of the fracture and the patient's age. A rehabilitation program then helps restore movement and strength.
items: Follow-up X-rays to confirm healing
Exercises to restore range of motion once the cast comes off
Nutrition advice to support bone health

image.alt: A leg supported by a cast while walking

services.title: Shoulder Pain
services.description: Assessing stiffness and pain in the shoulder and setting out the treatment options.

details.lead: The shoulder is one of the most mobile joints in the body, which makes it prone to problems such as tendinitis, rotator cuff injuries and frozen shoulder. An accurate diagnosis determines the right treatment.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The examination assesses range of motion and strength in different directions, along with specific tests for the tendons and ligaments.
An ultrasound or MRI may be requested when needed to assess the tendons and soft tissues.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Pain when you raise your arm or lie on your shoulder
A gradual loss of shoulder movement
Weakness when lifting objects
Pain after a previous injury or dislocation

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: Therapeutic exercises to restore movement and strengthen the muscles
Medication to ease pain and inflammation
Joint injections in selected cases
Discussing surgery for certain tendon injuries or instability

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: The shoulder usually needs a regular rehabilitation program, and full improvement can take longer than in some other joints — so sticking with the exercises is essential.
items: Daily home exercises
Follow-up to measure gains in range of motion
A gradual return to overhead activities

image.alt: A hands-on examination of the shoulder joint

services.title: Osteoarthritis
services.description: A complete plan for managing osteoarthritis and reducing its impact on everyday movement.

details.lead: Osteoarthritis is a long-term condition in which joint cartilage gradually wears down. With early diagnosis and the right plan, pain can be eased, movement improved and quality of life maintained.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: It most often affects the knees, hips, hands and spine, and becomes more common with age, excess weight or previous injuries.
Diagnosis is based on your symptoms, the clinical examination and X-rays, and treatment depends on how advanced the condition is and how it affects your daily life.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Joint pain that worsens with activity and eases with rest
Stiffness in the morning or after sitting for a while
Grinding or crackling when the joint moves
A gradual decline in your ability to walk or climb stairs

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: Strengthening and flexibility exercises
Weight management to reduce the load on the joints
Pain-relief medication
Joint injections in selected cases
Discussing surgical options at advanced stages

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: Osteoarthritis needs long-term follow-up. The aim is to control symptoms and preserve movement, adjusting the plan as your needs change.
items: Regular follow-up of your symptoms
A suitable physical activity program
Walking aids when needed to reduce the load

image.alt: Hands feeling the finger joints

services.title: Hand and Wrist
services.description: Diagnosing pain in the hand, wrist and fingers, and following the recovery of their function.

details.lead: Hand and wrist problems directly affect everyday tasks. They include carpal tunnel syndrome, tendinitis, fractures and ligament injuries.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The assessment checks sensation, grip strength and the movement of the fingers and wrist, with nerve conduction studies or imaging requested when needed.
The plan is designed to restore the function of your hand at work and in daily life.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Numbness or tingling in the fingers, especially at night
A weak grip or dropping objects
Wrist pain or swelling after a fall
Pain when moving the thumb or fingers
A finger that locks or is hard to straighten

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: A splint or night brace
Changing the activities that strain the hand
Hand therapy exercises
Local injections in selected cases
Discussing surgery when needed

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: Many hand and wrist problems improve with conservative treatment, while surgical cases need rehabilitation to restore movement and strength.
items: Daily hand exercises
Follow-up of sensation and strength
Advice on a hand-friendly work setup

image.alt: An X-ray of the bones of the wrist and hand

services.title: Foot and Ankle
services.description: Treating foot and ankle pain and recurrent sprains, and improving stability as you move.

details.lead: Your feet and ankles carry your body weight with every step, so problems such as recurrent sprains, heel pain and tendinitis have a big impact on daily movement.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The examination looks at how you walk, the shape of your foot, the stability of your ankle and where the pain is, with imaging when needed.
The plan aims to ease pain, improve stability and reduce the chance of the injury coming back.

sections.title: When you may need this service
items: Heel pain, especially with your first steps in the morning
Repeated ankle sprains
Swelling that persists after an injury
Pain that worsens with walking or long periods of standing
A change in the shape of the foot or toes

sections.title: Possible treatment options
items: Stretching and strengthening exercises
Choosing suitable footwear and foot supports
Temporary support with an ankle brace
Pain-relief medication
Discussing surgery for chronic instability or severe injuries

sections.title: Recovery and follow-up
paragraphs: Most patients improve gradually with regular exercise and suitable footwear, and ligament injuries need balance training to reduce repeat sprains.
items: Balance and stability exercises
A gradual return to walking and sport
Follow-up to review progress

image.alt: Fitting a foot and ankle brace

conditions.title: Joint Pain
conditions.excerpt: Ongoing or recurring pain in one or more joints that affects movement or sleep and needs an assessment to find its cause.

details.lead: Joint pain is a common symptom that can come from overuse, injury, inflammation or wear — and finding the cause is the most important step in choosing the right treatment.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The pain may affect one joint or several. It can be short-lived after exertion, or persistent enough to affect movement and sleep.
Describing what the pain feels like, when it happens and what comes with it helps guide the examination and the diagnosis.

sections.title: Possible causes
items: Overuse or repetitive strain on the joint
Injuries and sprains
Osteoarthritis
Inflammation of the tendons or bursae
Inflammatory conditions that need specialist assessment

sections.title: When to see a doctor
items: Pain lasting more than two weeks
Swelling, redness or warmth in the joint
Pain that stops you moving or sleeping
Pain together with fever or general fatigue

sections.title: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: Treatment depends on the cause. It may include relative rest, therapeutic exercise and suitable medication, with regular follow-up to make sure you are improving.

image.alt: A person sitting on the floor holding their ankle in pain

conditions.title: Back Pain
conditions.excerpt: Pain in the lower or upper back that lasts for days or spreads down the leg — especially with numbness or weakness.

details.lead: Back pain is one of the most common reasons to see an orthopedic doctor. Most cases are minor and improve, but some warning signs call for a prompt assessment.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The pain may be in the lower or upper back, and it can spread to the legs when it is linked to an irritated nerve.
How you sit and work, and how active you are, play a big part in how back pain starts and whether it returns.

sections.title: Possible causes
items: Muscle strain or overuse
Sitting in a poor posture for long periods
A herniated disc
Wear and tear in the spine
Lifting heavy objects incorrectly

sections.title: When to see a doctor
items: Pain spreading to the leg with numbness or weakness
Pain after a fall or accident
Pain that gets worse at night or at rest
Difficulty controlling your bladder or bowels — go to the emergency department immediately

sections.title: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: Treatment usually starts with conservative measures — exercise, adjusting your activities and suitable medication — with further imaging if there are nerve-related signs or no improvement.

image.alt: A woman with her hand on her lower back in pain

conditions.title: Sports Injuries
conditions.excerpt: Sprains, tears or sudden injuries during physical activity that should be examined before you return to training.

details.lead: Sports injuries are caused by sudden movements, contact or repetitive strain. An early assessment shows how serious the injury is and helps stop it from getting worse.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Common injuries include ankle sprains, knee ligament injuries, muscle tears and tendinitis.
Going back to training before you have fully recovered is one of the main reasons injuries come back.

sections.title: Possible causes
items: A sudden twist or turn of the joint
A collision or fall during play
Too little warm-up or overtraining
Increasing the training load too quickly

sections.title: When to see a doctor
items: Difficulty putting weight on the limb
Rapid swelling after the injury
A popping sound at the moment of injury
A feeling that the joint is unstable

sections.title: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: Care starts with first aid and an assessment to identify the type of injury, followed by a gradual rehabilitation program for a safe return to activity.

image.alt: A player helping a teammate with a knee injury during a match

conditions.title: Joint Stiffness and Osteoarthritis
conditions.excerpt: Morning stiffness or a gradual loss of movement can be early signs of osteoarthritis.

details.lead: Joint stiffness, especially in the morning, can be an early sign of osteoarthritis — and early care helps keep you moving.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Osteoarthritis develops slowly. It often begins with stiffness and pain after exertion, and may gradually limit movement.
An active lifestyle and the right exercises can ease the symptoms noticeably.

sections.title: Possible causes
items: Cartilage wear with age
Excess weight
Previous joint injuries
Genetic factors

sections.title: When to see a doctor
items: Morning stiffness that returns every day
Less movement in the joint than before
Pain that affects walking or work
Swelling in the joint that keeps coming back

sections.title: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: Treatment focuses on easing pain and improving movement through exercise, weight management and suitable medication, with other options considered at advanced stages.

image.alt: An anatomical drawing of the knee joint

conditions.title: Herniated Disc
conditions.excerpt: Part of a spinal disc bulges between the vertebrae and can press on a nerve, causing pain that spreads to the arm or leg.

details.lead: A herniated disc happens when part of the disc between two vertebrae bulges out and may press on a nerve root, causing radiating pain and numbness.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: It most often occurs in the lower back or neck, and many cases improve with conservative treatment within weeks to months.
A neurological examination — with an MRI when needed — shows where the disc has herniated and how much it affects the nerves.

sections.title: Possible causes
items: Age-related changes in the discs
Lifting heavy objects incorrectly
Sitting for long periods
Excess weight and weak core muscles

sections.title: When to see a doctor
items: Pain spreading to the leg or arm that doesn't improve
Numbness or weakness in a limb that is getting worse
Difficulty walking or standing
Loss of bladder or bowel control — go to the emergency department immediately

sections.title: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: Treatment usually starts with medication, therapeutic exercise and activity changes. Surgery is discussed if nerve compression persists or weakness increases.

image.alt: A woman holding her lower back with both hands

conditions.title: Frozen Shoulder
conditions.excerpt: Pain followed by gradual stiffness that limits shoulder movement in every direction, and usually improves with time and regular treatment.

details.lead: Frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis) is a condition in which the lining of the shoulder joint becomes inflamed and gradually stiffens, reducing movement and causing pain.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: It usually passes through stages: increasing pain, then stiffness, then a gradual return of movement.
It is more common in people with diabetes and after long periods of limited shoulder movement.

sections.title: Possible causes
items: Inflammation of the shoulder joint capsule
Little shoulder movement after an injury or surgery
Diabetes and thyroid disorders
No clear cause in some cases

sections.title: When to see a doctor
items: Shoulder pain that keeps you from sleeping
Difficulty brushing your hair or getting dressed
Shoulder movement that keeps decreasing

sections.title: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: Treatment aims to ease the pain and restore movement gradually with stretching exercises and physiotherapy; local injections may be used in selected cases.

image.alt: A specialist pressing on a patient's shoulder during a manual therapy session

conditions.title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
conditions.excerpt: Pressure on the median nerve at the wrist that causes numbness in the fingers and a weaker grip, often worse at night.

details.lead: Carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by pressure on the median nerve as it passes through a narrow tunnel at the wrist, leading to numbness and pain in the hand.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: People often feel numbness in the thumb, index and middle fingers, and may wake at night because of it.
A clinical examination — with nerve conduction studies when needed — confirms the diagnosis and shows how severe the compression is.

sections.title: Possible causes
items: Repetitive hand and wrist movements
Pregnancy and hormonal changes
Diabetes and an underactive thyroid
Previous wrist injuries or fractures

sections.title: When to see a doctor
items: Numbness that keeps returning or wakes you up
Weakness when gripping objects
Shrinking of the muscles at the base of the thumb

sections.title: Diagnosis and treatment
paragraphs: The plan usually starts with a night splint, activity changes and exercises. Local injections may be used, and surgery is discussed if symptoms persist or are severe.

image.alt: A woman holding her wrist and palm in pain

conditions.title: Osteoporosis
conditions.excerpt: A gradual loss of bone density that makes bones more likely to break, often with no symptoms until a fracture happens.

details.lead: Osteoporosis is a condition in which bone density falls and bone structure weakens, so bones break more easily — even after a minor fall.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: It is sometimes called a “silent disease” because it may cause no symptoms until the first fracture, often in the wrist, hip or spine.
A bone density scan helps diagnose it early and estimate the risk of fractures.

sections.title: Possible causes

faqs.question: How can I book an appointment?
faqs.answer: You can book by phone or on WhatsApp. We'll confirm a time that suits you and let you know about any instructions before your visit.

faqs.answer: Please bring any previous X-rays or test results, a list of the medicines you take, and any medical reports related to your current complaint.

faqs.answer: It depends on your condition. The aim is always to give you enough time to explain your complaint and understand your treatment plan.

articles.title: Knee Osteoarthritis: Early Symptoms and How to Manage Them
articles.excerpt: A simple guide to knee osteoarthritis: how it starts, the early signs you shouldn't ignore, and what you can do every day to ease the pain and stay mobile.

body.text: Knee osteoarthritis is one of the most common joint problems, especially after the age of forty. It happens when the cartilage that covers the ends of the bones inside the joint gradually wears away, so the joint loses some of its smoothness and its ability to absorb shock.
How does knee osteoarthritis start?
Osteoarthritis develops slowly over years. At first you may notice only mild pain after exertion or climbing stairs; clearer symptoms appear as the condition progresses.
Early signs

items: Knee pain that gets worse with long walks or stairs and eases with rest
Stiffness in the morning or after sitting for a while that improves within minutes of moving
A clicking or grinding sound when you bend the knee
Mild swelling around the joint that keeps coming back

body.text: What raises the risk?

items: Getting older
Excess weight, since every step multiplies the load on the knee
Previous knee injuries, such as a meniscus or ligament tear
Weak muscles around the knee
Genetic factors

body.text: What can you do every day?

items: Stay active: moderate walking, swimming and stationary cycling suit most people
Strengthen your thigh muscles with simple exercises — they take load off the joint
Keep to a healthy weight; even losing a few kilograms can ease the pain
Wear comfortable, supportive shoes
Spread your activity through the day and avoid very long spells of standing or sitting

body.title: Tip
body.text: Don't stop moving altogether because of pain — inactivity weakens the muscles and makes stiffness worse. Choose a suitable activity and build up gradually.
When should you see a doctor?

It's worth getting assessed if the pain lasts more than a few weeks, keeps coming back with swelling, or affects your sleep or your ability to walk. A clinical examination and X-rays show how advanced the osteoarthritis is and help set a suitable treatment plan, which may include therapeutic exercise and medication, with other options in advanced cases.

image.alt: A woman holding her knee while seated

articles.title: Lower Back Pain: Common Causes and When to Worry
articles.excerpt: Most lower back pain is minor and improves within weeks, but some signs call for a medical assessment. Learn the common causes and the right steps to take.

body.text: Most people have lower back pain at some point in their lives. The good news is that most cases are linked to strained muscles or ligaments, and they improve gradually with the right kind of movement and simple care.
Common causes

items: A muscle strain after lifting something heavy or a sudden movement
Sitting for long periods in a poor posture
Weak abdominal and back muscles
A herniated disc
Age-related changes in the vertebrae and discs

body.text: What to do in the first few days

items: Avoid complete bed rest — gentle movement helps you recover faster
Use warm compresses to relax tight muscles
Modify painful activities for a while instead of stopping everything
Check with your doctor before taking painkillers, especially if you have a long-term condition

body.title: Signs that need urgent assessment
body.text: See a doctor immediately if back pain comes with increasing weakness in your legs, numbness around the pelvis, difficulty controlling your bladder or bowels, an unexplained fever, or if the pain started after a fall or accident.
Prevention is better than cure

Strengthening your core muscles, keeping to a healthy weight, taking short movement breaks during desk work, and lifting with your knees bent rather than bending your back all help reduce the chance of the pain coming back.
When should you see an orthopedic doctor?

If the pain lasts more than four to six weeks despite care at home, spreads down your leg, or keeps returning in a way that affects your work and daily life, a medical assessment helps find the cause and set a suitable treatment plan.

image.alt: A specialist examining the lower back of a patient lying down

articles.title: First Aid for Sports Injuries: What to Do in the First Few Minutes
articles.excerpt: The first minutes after a sports injury make a real difference to recovery. Practical steps for sprains and bruises, and when to stop and get checked.

body.text: Sports injuries happen at every level of play, from friendly matches to competitions. Handling them correctly in the first few minutes reduces swelling and pain and supports a better recovery.
Stop playing straight away
Playing on after an injury can turn a minor problem into a more serious one. If you feel sudden pain, hear a pop or no longer trust a joint to hold, stop and get it assessed.
First aid for sprains and bruises

items: Rest: stop putting weight on the injured limb
Ice: apply a cold pack wrapped in a cloth for 15 to 20 minutes, and repeat every few hours on the first day
Compression: use a compression bandage firmly, but not too tightly
Elevation: raise the injured limb above the level of your heart to reduce swelling

body.title: Never put ice directly on the skin
body.text: Always wrap ice in a cloth to avoid a cold injury to the skin, and don't go beyond the recommended time for each application.
Signs that you need to see a doctor

items: Difficulty walking or putting weight on the limb after the injury
An obvious deformity of the joint or bone
Severe, rapid swelling
Numbness or coldness in the injured limb
Pain that doesn't improve within a few days

body.text: Getting back to play

Don't rely on the pain going away as your only sign that you're ready. Your muscles and ligaments first need to regain their strength, flexibility and balance, and a gradual rehabilitation program helps you return safely and lowers the risk of re-injury.

image.alt: An injured footballer lying on the pitch while a teammate checks on him

articles.title: Osteoporosis: How to Protect Your Bones at Every Age
articles.excerpt: Osteoporosis often shows no symptoms until the first fracture. Learn about the risk factors, the role of diet and exercise, and when a bone density scan is recommended.

body.text: Bone mass is built up during childhood and early adulthood, and then slowly declines with age. When that decline speeds up, bones become weaker and more likely to break — the condition known as osteoporosis.
Why is it called a “silent disease”?
Because it often causes no pain or obvious symptoms until a bone breaks — often in the wrist, hip or spine, sometimes after only a minor fall.
What raises the risk of osteoporosis?

items: Getting older, especially for women after menopause
A family history of osteoporosis or hip fractures
Too little calcium and vitamin D
Physical inactivity
Smoking
Long-term use of some medicines, such as steroids

body.text: Steps to protect your bones

items: Include calcium-rich foods in your diet, such as dairy products and leafy greens
Get moderate sun exposure, and ask your doctor whether you need vitamin D supplements
Do weight-bearing exercise such as walking and light resistance training
Avoid smoking and cut down on high-caffeine drinks
Make your home safer from falls, with good lighting and non-slip floors

body.title: Bone density scans
body.text: A bone density scan helps detect osteoporosis early, before any fractures happen. Ask your doctor when it's right for you based on your age and risk factors.
Treatment is possible
If osteoporosis is confirmed, treatment plans combine diet, exercise and suitable medication, as assessed by the doctor, to lower the risk of fractures and maintain quality of life.

image.alt: The clasped hands of an older person

articles.title: Sitting Well at Your Desk: A Practical Guide to Protecting Your Back and Neck
articles.excerpt: Long hours at a screen are a major cause of back and neck pain. Simple changes to your workspace and daily habits can make a big difference.

body.text: Many of us spend long hours every day at a computer or on our phones, and over time a poor posture can turn into lasting pain in the neck, shoulders and lower back.
Set up your workspace

items: Place the top of the screen at or slightly below eye level, about an arm's length away
Choose a chair that supports your lower back, or put a small cushion behind you
Keep your feet flat on the floor and your knees at roughly a right angle
Keep the keyboard and mouse close, so your elbows stay by your sides
If you use a laptop for long periods, add a stand and a separate keyboard

body.text: Keep moving regularly
The best posture is your next one — the body doesn't like staying still for long, even in a good position. Change position often and take a short movement break every 30 to 45 minutes.
Simple exercises at work

items: Gently draw your chin back to lengthen your neck, and repeat ten times
Lift your shoulders toward your ears, then slowly let them drop
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a few seconds
Stand up and walk for two minutes, or climb a few stairs

body.title: Watch your phone posture
body.text: Looking down at your phone with your head bent forward increases the load on your neck. Raise the phone to eye level whenever you can.
When should you see a doctor?
If the pain continues after you've improved your work posture, or comes with numbness in your arms or frequent headaches, a medical assessment helps find the cause and the right treatment.

image.alt: A woman working on a laptop while sitting in an ergonomic office chair

articles.title: Physiotherapy After an Injury: Why Rest Alone Isn't Enough
articles.excerpt: Rest is part of recovery, but it isn't everything. Learn how physiotherapy helps restore movement and strength, and how to get the most from your sessions.

body.text: After an injury, a fracture or surgery, many people assume that rest alone will be enough to recover. But long periods of inactivity can weaken muscles and stiffen joints — and that is where physiotherapy comes in.
What does physiotherapy offer?

items: Gradually restoring the joint's range of motion
Strengthening muscles weakened by the injury or by inactivity
Improving balance and movement control to reduce the risk of re-injury
Relieving pain with techniques chosen by your therapist
Teaching you home exercises that build on your sessions

body.text: The stages of rehabilitation

items: Protecting the injured area and easing pain and swelling
Restoring movement and flexibility
Gradual strengthening
Returning to daily or sporting activities

body.text: How long each stage takes depends on the type and severity of the injury, and your doctor and therapist will decide when you're ready to move on to the next one.

body.title: Home exercises are essential
body.text: Sessions alone aren't enough — keeping up your home exercises between sessions is one of the most important factors in a successful recovery.
How to get the most from your sessions

items: Keep to your session schedule and your home exercises
Tell your therapist about any unusual pain during exercise
Don't rush back to full activity before the agreed time
Note your progress and any difficulties to discuss at follow-up

image.alt: A physiotherapist helping a patient through a stretching exercise

articles.title: When Do You Need an MRI? A Simple Guide for Patients
articles.excerpt: Not every bone or joint pain needs an MRI. Learn how the types of imaging differ, when your doctor may request an MRI, and how to prepare for one.

body.text: With modern scans so widely available, many patients ask about an MRI at their very first visit. But the most suitable test depends on your complaint and on what the clinical examination finds — not every pain needs an MRI.
How the types of imaging differ

items: Plain X-rays: best for assessing bones, fractures and osteoarthritis
Ultrasound: useful for assessing some tendons and tissues close to the skin
MRI: shows soft tissues in detail, such as cartilage, ligaments, spinal discs and nerves
CT scans: give detailed images of bone in certain cases

body.text: When might your doctor request an MRI?

items: A suspected ligament or cartilage injury inside a joint
Back or neck pain with nerve-related signs such as numbness or weakness
No improvement despite an adequate period of treatment
The need for precise planning before a treatment procedure

body.text: How to prepare for an MRI

items: Tell your doctor if you have a pacemaker, any implanted device or metal fragments in your body
Remove jewelry, watches and other metal items before the scan
Let the team know if you are pregnant or uneasy in enclosed spaces
Keep still during the scan so the images are clear

body.title: Results are read alongside the examination
body.text: An MRI can show normal age-related changes that don't cause any pain, so results are always interpreted in light of your symptoms and the clinical examination — never on their own.
If you have previous scans, bring them to your visit; they may spare you a repeat test or help compare changes over time.
